Question: On a certain math exam, \(10\%\) of the students got \(70\) points, \(25\%\) got \(80\) points, \(20\%\) got \(85\) points, \(15\%\) got \(90\) points, and the rest got \(95\) points. What is the difference between the mean and the median score on this exam?
Solution:
The percentages describe how much each score contributes to the mean. The percentage scoring \(95\) is
\[
100\%-(10\%+25\%+20\%+15\%)=30\%.
\]
Multiplying each score by its fraction of the students gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{mean}&=0.10(70)+0.25(80)+0.20(85)\\
&\quad+0.15(90)+0.30(95)\\
&=86.
\end{aligned}
\]
To find the median, imagine the scores arranged from least to greatest. Exactly \(35\%\) are below \(85\), while \(55\%\) are at most \(85\). Thus the middle score is \(85\); if there are two middle scores, both lie in the block of \(85\)s. The median is therefore \(85\).

The difference is \(86-85=1\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
